paper.abstract_en: The detailed excitation functions for <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>13</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> elastic scattering and the additional thick target inverse kinematics measurements were analyzed using the <math><mi>R</mi></math> matrix approach. The analysis covered the excitation region in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> from 8.6 up to 11.2 MeV. Information on single particle widths of the levels in the <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus and shell model calculations are in good agreement. A comparative analysis of the <math><mi>α</mi></math>-cluster structures of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nuclei indicates their common underlying nature. However, the structure in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is more complex. In particular, each <math><mi>α</mi></math>-cluster level with spin <math><mi>J</mi></math> in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></math> corresponds to several levels with spins <math><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. Unexpectedly, the reduced-width-weighted centroids of the higher-spin members of these doublets always lie at lower excitation energies in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math>.
